quote_text:
Another win here, a good three points.  I'm disappointed with the goal we lost,  
but really good reaction from us. I had to  change it midway through the first half,  
tactically. I knew that Dundee United were  going to come and set everybody behind the  
ball and try and frustrate us. But in the past,  it’s something that Rangers have struggled with.  
So we tweaked it a wee bit, we had a wee chat  at half-time, we spoke through a few things,  
and then the second half, just as the  game went on, we got the second goal,  
we finished it really strongly, and we  could have had another couple of goals.
Goals for Dessers—what can you say about him? I'm delighted for him because I think the big  
man comes in for unfair criticism. I really  do. But to work with him the last three months,  
I see how much effort he puts in on the training  field. He works really hard at his game, he gives  
you everything. And it’s a brilliant return this  year—28 goals. But when we got that penalty,  
normally it’s the skip—the skipper, sorry—that  goes up and takes them. I’m thinking to myself,  
“He better score this or he’s going to get  one from me,” but thankfully he hit the  
back of the net. So yeah, I’m delighted  for him, and it’s a brilliant return.
They were singing your name at  the end—what does that mean? 
It means a lot because it’s a club that  I've been at since I was, what, seven,  
eight years old. And yeah, I’m not scared  to say it—it was a bit emotional. But look,  
since I've come in, I’ve given it everything. I  said in my first interview I was going to be me,  
I wasn’t going to try and kid  anybody on. I have been me. So yep,  
really enjoyed it. It was good to get  that reception, but we've still got one  
game to go on Saturday against Hibs at Easter  Road, so all focus needs to go on that now.
You brought Jack back into the team today.  There’s been a lot of focus this season,  
but you must be pleased with the  way he performed in the first half. 
Yeah, it was always my intention to bring  Jack back in at some stage. Firstly,  
Liam Kelly has been excellent—top class—but  over the last two or three weeks he’s had a  
niggle in his back which he’s been  carrying. But I was going to bring,  
as I said, Jack back in. I decided  to bring him back in tonight. Look,  
it’s been a tough period for Jack, but I’ve been  honest with him. I think if you ask him himself,  
he'll tell you that. But you’ve seen his  qualities tonight, and I was delighted for him.
So that’s the problem next season now—Rangers have  two quality number ones fighting for that spot. 
You still believe he's got the mindset, the  quality to be Rangers number one next season? 
Jack? Yep. Jack and Liam. Jack and Liam—one  thing I will say about Jack is, when I made  
the decision, his attitude has been first class.  So that sums him up as a man first and foremost,  
because it's not easy when, as a manager, you  sit an experienced player down and tell him  
that he’s obviously not going to be playing.  I looked in his eyes and he was disappointed,  
but listen, his reaction has been brilliant  in training. He’s given it everything  
because he knows he’s up against Liam, who  since he’s come in has been excellent as  
well. And you saw it—you saw when I brought  him in against Beale, who was the first man  
over to him? Jack Butland. So delighted for  Jack. That was the Jack that I know. And  
I just thought it was the right thing to  do, but delighted with his performance.
Dessers—when he came off, it looked  as if he was saying goodbye to the  
fans. Is it highly unlikely we’ll  see him back here next season? 
No, he was brought off because he was tired.  That’s why I brought him off. And listen,  
he’s loved it here. I’ve got a really good  relationship with Dessers. Who knows what's  
going to happen going forward? But one thing  about Dessers—he’s been a top operator for  
Rangers this year. And he’s loved it. You just  never know what's going to happen in the future.
Last one, Barry, just on your own  personal reflections. It’s been  
a rollercoaster three months—what's your  biggest takeaway from your time in the job? 
My biggest takeaway is I’ve got a few more  wrinkles. I've got a few more grey hairs, that’s  
for sure. But listen, I’ve loved every minute of  it. I knew it wasn’t going to be perfect when I  
came in, but I was willing to take that challenge  on. And it has had its challenges—believe me,  
it’s been challenging. But as I said, every  day I drive into that training centre,  
every day I walk through the front doors,  it’s a privilege to be here and work here. And  
it’s not over yet, so we've still got one game.  And you never know what’s around the corner.
Thanks, guys.
title: 'It was emotional' | Full Barry Ferguson Post Match Press Conference | Rangers 3-1 Dundee United
